correctness.rationale: For R(s,x)=(as+f(x),su+Ax), the (t,v) identity gives f(A+aI)=0 and A²=−u⊗f. On V×V the t-component cancels and both V-components equal f(v)Aw−f(w)Av; the (t,t) identity is automatic. This reduction works in characteristic two. If f≠0, A preserves ker f and squares to zero there, hence vanishes there since ker f is a line. Thus A=w⊗f, f(w)=−a, u=aw, and R is the rank-one map (1,w)⊗(a,f). For every nonzero f there are q choices of a and q choices of w, giving q⁴−q² rank-one maps. For f=0 there are q² square-zero A, counting the nonzero ones by their common image/kernel line and a nonzero quotient-to-line map. For A=0 the free first column gives one zero and q³−1 rank-one maps; each nonzero A gives q rank-one maps (a=0 and u in the image) and q³−q rank-two maps. Summing yields the stated ranks and total, with rank three impossible by the same argument over every field. Substitution q→q^m in the counts and the defining exponential series give the zeta function. A separate basis-pair bracket enumeration of all 512 matrices over F₂ gave (1,25,18,0); the uploaded artifacts/verify.py was inspected, not run. This enumeration checks F₂ only, not the arbitrary-field identity or general count.
